transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Ava Morales (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Redwood PM), Theo Ramos (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (MoonPort CTO), Riya Shah (MoonPort Infra), Marco Diaz (MoonPort Security), Juno Lee (MoonPort Platform)

Summary: Quick technical alignment on the hybrid connector and marketplace listing authz flow. Discussed KMS integration patterns, helm operator compatibility, container image signing, canary rollout strategy for listing, and pilot run logistics. Several action items captured.

Topics: hybrid connector auth, KMS/audit, helm operator & k8s compat, network egress rules, image signing & SBOM, pilot plan and acceptance criteria

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. We'll do a technical alignment, try to keep to 55, 60 ish. Liam will drive the deep bits. Quick intros?
[00:10] Ethan (MoonPort): Hi, I'm Ethan, CTO at MoonPort. We're focused on payments routing and had a spike about hosting some inference at the edge for routing decisions.
[00:18] Riya (MoonPort): Riya here, infra eng, I manage our k8s clusters and networking.
[00:22] Marco (MoonPort): Marco, security architect, I'll own the audit and compliance questions.
[00:26] Ava: Great — Liam?
[00:28] Liam (Redwood SE): Liam here, I handle integration for marketplace connectors and the helm operator. I'll cover how Redwood's private listing works and the auth flows.
[00:34] Theo (Redwood): Theo — I'll surface any SDK or rollout notes.
[00:37] Juno (MoonPort): Juno, platform, will be the primary contact for pilots.
[00:40] 
[02:00] Liam: Ok, quick architecture overview. For a hybrid listing we typically have a small managed control plane in Redwood and a customer-managed runtime — either VPC or on-prem. We'll talk about the connector (daemonset or helm operator) that establishes mTLS to our control plane, and the KMS flow for key wrapping.
[02:20] Riya: Quick Q — does the connector require outbound internet egress? Our policy is extremely restrictive, we only allow certain CIDRs.
[02:26] Liam: Yes, by default the connector initiates outbound on port 443 to the redwood control endpoints. We can scope to specific IP ranges and support proxying through a customer egress gateway. Also, we can do an enterprise peered VPC where traffic stays in-cloud.
[02:42] Ethan: Curious about latency — if we run a model in our region via the connector, how much extra hop/handshake overhead is added? We need to keep routing under 60ms typically.
[02:50] Liam: Good point. There are two patterns: pinned local runtime where inference stays in your VPC — minimal added latency (tens of ms mostly around TLS). The other is our dedicated hosted fallback which adds more latency. For pilot, we'd recommend local runtime. Also note that initial model load / KV cache fill will spike latency.
[03:12] Marco: On KMS — we use CloudKMS with CMEK. We need a model for envelope keys so Redwood never persists unwrapped keys. Do you have an example flow?
[03:20] Liam: Yep. Our pattern: customer KMS issues a data-encryption-key (DEK) which is wrapped by the customer's KMS key and only the wrapped blob is stored. At runtime the wrapped DEK is unwrapped within customer-owned enclave or node using the customer KMS, never exported. We have a KMS integration playbook we can share.
[03:36] Marco: Good. Also need audit logs for every unwrap, key access, and model version changes.
[03:42] Liam: We emit audit events to the control-plane's audit stream; for private deployments we can forward logs to your syslog or cloud logging endpoint, or provide signed event webhooks.
[03:51] Marco: Signed events, yes. We need tamper-evidence.
[03:54] Liam: We support HMAC-signed webhooks and event sequencing; we'll include the schema in the playbook.
[04:10] 
[06:00] Sofia (Redwood PM): Acceptance criteria idea for pilot: must run a 1-hour traffic replay with 95th p90 latency < 120ms, token unit cost below the threshold, and audit logs showing unwrap events. Thoughts?
[06:12] Ethan: That sounds fair. We need to confirm the traffic replay tooling can simulate our routing blasts — we'll share a snippet.
[06:20] Juno: We'll also need canary rollback strategy — if a model or quantized variant regresses quality we need automatic fallback to prior model. Does Redwood support automatic fallback?
[06:30] Liam: Yes — rollout policies allow canary percent and automatic fallback on error or quality regression. We can wire in your eval hooks or use Redwood's built-in eval triggers. There was a small doc we sent earlier (link: https://redwood.ai/pilot-rollouts) — Ava will re-share.
[06:48] 
[08:00] Riya: About the helm operator — we're on k8s 1.26, constrained nodes, and use Privatized CRI. Any known compatibility issues?
[08:10] Liam: Our helm operator supports 1.22+, but some CRI features require the node to have ephemeral storage and sufficient mmap limits for large KV caches. For constrained nodes we can run the runtime on separate pool with gpu or cpu optimizations. Also, if you don't want the operator we have a daemonset container image option.
[08:34] Riya: Hmm daemonset might be preferable first. Can you produce small images and signed manifests? We need image signing (cosign) and SBOMs.
[08:41] Liam: Yes, we publish cosign-signed images and SBOMs for every release. For hybrid listing we can publish a release tag specifically for your onboarding.
[09:00] Marco: How do you handle model artifacts — are model weights ever staged in Redwood?
[09:06] Liam: Two choices: 1) model stored in Redwood object storage encrypted with your DEK (wrapped) and pulled into your runtime at startup, or 2) you host model artifacts in your own s3 and we pull from there. For max compliance, option 2 is recommended.
[09:22] Ethan: We prefer option 2 to control residency. Performance implications?
[09:27] Liam: Slightly more complexity at startup (prewarm stage) but runtime performance is the same once model loaded. We'll provide a prewarm script to warm KV cache.
[09:36] 
[11:00] Theo: On routing — if capacity is constrained we can route to a smaller quantized variant. Does MoonPort want auto-quant routing?
[11:08] Riya: We are cautious because quant variants have different latency/quality tradeoffs. We want to do canary evaluation and manual gating first.
[11:15] Liam: Sure — we can do manual gating and include rollout labels. The runtime also tracks quality regressions by token-level diffs if you feed eval sets.
[11:26] 
[13:00] Marco: Audit & SSO — we'd like SAML SSO federation for the console and RBAC for team separation. Also, SOC2 docs.
[13:10] Ava: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we have role templates for infra, sec, and dev. We'll share SOC2 type II and pen test summaries in the security pack.
[13:24] Marco: Please anonymize any third-party cloud account IDs when you send the pack.
[13:28] Ava: Yep, noted.
[13:35] 
[15:00] Liam: Quick demo idea for pilot: 1) deploy runtime via daemonset in your staging cluster; 2) point runtime at your s3 for model files; 3) run a 30-minute replay at low qps to validate function; 4) perform a 1-hour full replay acceptance test. We'll provide a spreadsheet for latency/costs.
[15:20] Juno: Can you add sample scripts for generating traffic and for KV warm?
[15:25] Liam: Absolutely — we'll include a traffic-replay script (bash/Python) and a prewarm script.
[15:32] 
[17:00] Ethan: About billing — will we be billed for tokens when model is hosted in our cluster? We want clarity if there's a control-plane charge vs runtime charge.
[17:08] Ava: For hybrid private listing there's a small control-plane fee plus runtime usage. For fully customer-hosted artifacts the per-token fee is lower; we'll sketch out options in the SOW.
[17:20] Ethan: Would love a sample cost model for our expected 1M tokens/day.
[17:24] Ava: We'll attach a sample cost sheet.
[17:28] 
[19:00] Riya: Networking specifics: we'll provide egress CIDRs and a staging kubeconfig. Any special iptables or calico rules required?
[19:08] Liam: No special rules, but the operator needs to pull images and access control-plane endpoints. If you use egress gateway, we'll work with you to open ports.
[19:20] Riya: Ok.
[19:24] 
[21:00] Marco: One more security note — supply chain: we require signed images, SBOM, and reproducible build notes for the operator.
[21:08] Liam: We publish SBOMs and reproducible-build metadata; cosign-signed artifacts are standard. We'll include build provenance.
[21:18] Marco: Great.
[21:22] 
[23:00] Ava: Let's recap next steps — Liam will run compat tests; Riya provides staging creds and CIDRs; Marco sends SOC2 scoping; Ava sends pilot SOW and pricing. We'll aim to start the pilot week of April 18th.
[23:20] Ethan: That works.
[23:24] Ava: Any blockers?
[23:28] Riya: None immediate.
[23:30] Marco: None.
[23:32] 
[25:00] Theo: I'll follow up on the webhook schema and the exact audit field names — expect that in the playbook.
[25:08] Liam: Also, a heads up: if you want air-gapped we have an on-prem bundle but that adds extra SOW items; we can discuss if needed.
[25:18] Ethan: We'll evaluate after the pilot.
[25:22] 
[55:00] Ava: Great — thanks everyone. We'll share notes and links.
[55:08] Juno: Thanks all.
[55:10] Meeting end.
